title: Context Kernel legacy connection ownership backfill

phases.objective: Backfill deterministic personal/company workspace ownership and unique legacy connection mappings without activating legacy provider connections or inventing provider-account identity.

e2e_journeys.entrypoint: Legacy workspaces and user_app_connections exist after Context Kernel ownership persistence.
e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: Only deterministic workspace classifications and uniquely resolved connection ownership mappings are persisted; legacy connections remain unclassified until governed reconnect supplies durable provider identity.
steps: Classify only personal or company workspaces from membership, grant, and brand-association evidence.
Resolve legacy grants using workspace_id or tenant_id resource_ref compatibility.
Persist a connection mapping only when exactly one workspace candidate exists.
Insert null provider-account binding fields with status unclassified.
Preserve existing explicit classifications and ownership rows on replay.
assertions: Brand scope is not inferred from a company workspace.
Provider account identity is not synthesized from email_key, account metadata, resource identifiers, targets, or credentials.
Backfilled legacy ownership cannot become runtime-usable until a later governed reconnect activates it.

phases.objective: Add governed readback summaries for classifications, mappings, skipped ambiguities, and reconnect-required connections.
Certify replay and concurrent reconnect behavior while preserving explicit ownership.
Apply only after production-parity governed dry-run evidence and review.
Require post-apply data readback before any legacy connection can be enabled through reconnect.
